name: Encoding Converter
description: Convert text between common character sets.

results.outputHint: The result can be copied directly.

hints.input: The input encoding says how the content is read as bytes; the source charset says what those bytes mean. Do not mix them up.
hints.bom: A byte order mark only makes sense for UTF-8 and UTF-16; enabling it writes the mark at the start of the output.
hints.output: The output is Base64 by default, which is handy when you need a byte string.

faq.q: Why do I see replacement characters?
faq.a: Characters that do not exist in the target charset cannot be mapped, so they are replaced by a placeholder and a lossy-conversion warning is raised.
It guesses from byte patterns and works well between UTF-8 and single-byte charsets; sibling sets such as GBK and Big5 are easy to confuse, so name the charset explicitly for important data.

faq.q: Why does UTF-16 have two byte orders?
faq.a: UTF-16 stores text either little-endian or big-endian. Writing UTF-16 emits a BOM so the reader can tell them apart.
